text:
maria: Heads-up — noticed a sharp drop in prefix cache hit-rate for the Structured JSON output path on canary v2. This looks tied to kernel selection churn + batching alignment. TL;DR: chat/RAG long-context workload: prefix hit 18% -> 6% over last 10k requests, kernel-swap spikes, and KV lookups show many near-misses.

alex: ugh. any obvious key diffs?

maria: quick sample from KV telemetry shows a lot of similar prefixes differing only in JSON whitespace and key order. also some tokens get locale-normalized differently (nbsp vs space).

sam: can you paste a small reproducer of the failing key pairs?

maria: sure — here are two actual prefix keys (sanitized) that miss each other:
```
{"user":"alice","query":"What are the pros of X?","context":[{"id":123}]}
{ "context": [ {"id":123}], "query":"What are the pros of X?","user":"alice" }
```
Both semantically same but different fingerprint -> separate cache entries.

nidhi: that explains a lot for structured outputs. We never canonicalize JSON for prefix keying. For chat completions (plain text) this wasn't visible.

toby: also noticed kernel-swap events increase when batch coalescer aligns across mixed request shapes. Kernel selection flips between quantized and fp16 paths and that seems to evict KV shards more often. Kernel swap rate: 0.2/s baseline -> 4.5/s during spike window.

alex: oof. So two orthogonal causes: key instability for structured outputs and eviction/thrash from kernel/batch changes. What's the immediate mitigation?

maria: proposed short-term mitigations:
- Add JSON canonicalization step to prefix keying: stable key order + strip insignificant whitespace + normalize unicode spaces.
- Pin kernel for canary model to avoid dynamic kernel swap while we test.
- Increase KV shard pin TTL on the node for 30m to reduce eviction noise.

sam: sounds good. Any perf cost for canonicalization? CPU microcost but we can do it async at proxy before crypto hash. Should be tiny relative to tokens served.

nidhi: we should be careful: some users rely on ordering for structured responses (rare) — canonicalization must be opt-in per model or only for prefix-keying (not for eval logs).

maria: agreed. plan: enable prefix-key JSON-normalize at proxy layer for structured-output models only (config flag). Turn off kernel swap for canary, run traffic for 6h, measure hit-rate and kernel-swap metrics.

toby: can we get a quick telemetry query to track hit-rate delta and kernel-swap per-host? I ran a quick one but here's a nicer one we can use in the dashboard:
```
select
  time_bin,
  sum(kv_hits) / sum(kv_lookups) as kv_hitrate,
  sum(kernel_swap_events) as swap_events
from telemetry.prefix_cache
where model in ("canary-v2-struct")
group by time_bin(5m)
order by time_bin
```
Link: https://dash.internal/redwood/heatmap/canary-v2-struct (internal)

alex: after normalization + pin kernel, what beat do we expect?

maria: conservative estimate: hit-rate back to ~16-18%. If key instability was the dominant cause, we might see >20%. If eviction was dominant we'll get partial recovery.

sam: what about batching? I think batch coalescer heuristics still produce incompatible prefix slots when mixed chat+RAG requests come in the same slot. Could we add affinity buckets so structured responses prefer same-shape batching?

toby: yes — affinity buckets are a follow-up. Short term we can tweak coalescer to avoid mixing structured and plain-text outputs within the same batch for 1 minute on canary.

maria: experiment plan summary:
1) Deploy proxy JSON-normalize flag for structured-output models (opt-in).
2) Pin kernel selection for canary-v2-struct for 6h.
3) Increase KV shard pin TTL to 30m on canary fleet.
4) Adjust batch coalescer to prefer shape-affinity for structured types.
5) Monitor kv_hitrate, swap_events, end-to-end p50/p95 token latency, and cost delta.

nidhi: add a regression/assertion in rollouts: fail canary if kv_hitrate drops >5% vs baseline or kernel_swap_events >2x.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: canary-v2-struct -> 3 nodes. ETA ~12m.

perf-bot: perf snapshot (pre-change): kv_hitrate=0.18, kernel_swap_rate=0.22/s, p95 token latency=110ms.

alex: thanks. I'll own the pin+coalescer tweak. sam — can you add canonicalize util in proxy (small lib + tests)? nidhi — update rollout gate. toby — monitor eviction counters.

sam: will open PR with tests and bench (should be <500ns per key).

toby: started a live watch: https://logs.internal/redwood/streams/xyz (monitoring link)

maria: nice. If we get hit-rate back up, we should later consider persistent canonicalization for structured models and upstream SDK helpers to encourage stable key generation (e.g., model-ordered key builders).

alex: also add a note in docs: "structured outputs may need key normalization to get cache benefits" so customers understand.

maria: cool — will post results here after 6h canary. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: perf snapshot (post-change, 2h): kv_hitrate=0.17 -> 0.19 (small), kernel_swap_rate=0.2/s -> 0.5/s (improved after pin), p95 token latency +3ms. Further tuning ongoing.
